title: US Formally Rescinds Syria's State Sponsor of Terrorism Designation
detail: The US State Department formally rescinded Syria's designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism (SST) on August 24, 2026, after the mandatory 45-day congressional notification period that followed President Trump's July 8 letter to Congress. Syria had held the designation since 1979; only Cuba, Iran, and North Korea remain listed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio simultaneously revoked the Specially Designated Global Terrorist designation for Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (formerly al-Nusrah Front), citing 'positive actions taken and further commitments' by President Ahmad al-Sharaa to distance Syria from international terrorism. President al-Sharaa called the decision 'historic,' and Syria's finance minister described it as a 'major and historic success for Syrian diplomacy' expected to ease reconstruction financing and banking access.

media.caption: US removes Syria from the state sponsors of terrorism list

title: Assad-Era Grand Mufti Ahmad Hassoun Sentenced to Life for War Crimes
detail: Damascus's Fourth Criminal Court sentenced Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun — Syria's grand mufti from 2005 to 2021 under Bashar al-Assad, nicknamed the 'barrel bomb mufti' — to life in prison on August 24, 2026, plus additional consecutive terms (20 years for inciting killings, 10 years for prolonging killings) and confiscation of his assets, after convicting him of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Judge Fakhr al-Din al-Aryan said the official religious establishment under Hassoun provided 'religious cover for military and security operations' and publicly justified barrel bombs used against civilian areas. Hassoun was arrested at Damascus airport in March 2025 after emerging from hiding, and is the first senior Sunni religious figure — rather than a regime military or security official — tried in Syria's transitional justice process.

media.caption: Ahmad Hassoun, Assad's 'barrel bomb mufti,' sentenced to life in prison
